stories.headline: Browser reply reader lands with unfinished return paths
stories.summary: A new read-only ChatGPT browser adapter landed on main to help CUSTODIAN orchestration collect completed replies. Code inspection finds debugging return paths that break its stated output contract; validation and live operation are not established.
stories.body: Commit f42cc51 adds get_chatgpt_response.py v1.1.0, attaching through an existing local Chrome debugging endpoint and reading visible conversation DOM. The implementation documents a strict completed-text / RESPONSE IN PROGRESS / error contract, but read_once currently returns 'FIRST DOT GET BUSY' when generation is active, returns a page object when reply text is empty, and emits a debugging placeholder on an unexpected probe result. These paths contradict the documented interface and may confuse orchestration consumers. This is a verified source-level defect, not proof of an observed runtime failure. No tests, independent acceptance, running process, or teardown were verified. The private pilot observation pointer was last modified earlier than this commit and is not fresh evidence of this state.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now has a browser-side reader intended to collect completed ChatGPT responses for its orchestration loop. The new script is on main, but its current source contains unfinished return paths that could mislead the next automation step.

sections.heading: A bridge from browser conversations to orchestration
sections.text: The adapter attaches to an existing Chrome debugging session, identifies a conversation and reads visible assistant text. It is designed to avoid private application APIs and report whether a reply has finished.

sections.heading: The contract and the code diverge
sections.text: The script promises either completed text, a standard in-progress marker, or a nonzero error. Instead, an active reply can return a debugging phrase; an empty reply can return a browser page object; and an unexpected probe state returns a placeholder. These are source-confirmed inconsistencies, not observed production failures.

insights.title: A small protocol mismatch can stall a large art pipeline
insights.explanation: An orchestrator needs reliable completion signals before fetching and installing generated assets. Ambiguous output can turn a finished response into a false success or a stuck handoff.

insights.title: Landing is not validation
insights.explanation: The commit proves the adapter exists on main. It does not establish tests, independent acceptance, or a running browser connection.

article.takeaway: The new bridge is a useful integration point, but its response contract needs correction and tests before consumers rely on it.
article.next_watch: Watch for a follow-up patch restoring the documented return values and a bounded test of completed, streaming, empty, and ambiguous replies.

stories.headline: In-game art flagging reaches draft review, promising coordinate-stamped field notes
stories.summary: Draft PR #111 proposes an opt-in I-key Art Inspector that records local screenshots and world coordinates, plus a read-only collector grouping missing-art flags. It is not merged, validated in Godot, or enabled in production.
stories.body: PR #111 introduces a proposed Art Field Notes workflow for recording missing art during gameplay. An opt-in I-key capture would save local PNG/JSON evidence with world coordinates and bounded visible actors; a Python collector groups flags by spatial stretch. Manifest instructions describe a human-approved, incremental installation lane. The PR is draft and explicitly requests Godot import and runtime smoke tests, privacy/security review and regression validation. It does not generate, approve or install art. Release-mode inspection currently requires broader DevMode flags, so a dedicated inspection-only gate is a material pre-release question. No passing CI or independent review was established. Main remains eef8a41f8e82fe47c346002087f52492d945322a.
bullets: Draft PR #111 proposes I-key coordinate-stamped local screenshot/JSON capture.

article.lead: A practical bridge between spotting missing artwork and fixing it has reached draft review. Art Field Notes would let a developer press I while playing CUSTODIAN, capture where the problem occurs, and later group nearby observations into manageable installation stretches.

sections.heading: From visual annoyance to actionable coordinates
sections.text: The proposed inspector records a local screenshot and JSON with world coordinates and a bounded view of nearby actors. A separate read-only collector groups flags by location so artwork can be matched to the correct manifest entry rather than guessed from memory.

sections.heading: Art approval stays deliberately separate
sections.text: The manifest adds a staged installation workflow, but neither the inspector nor collector approves images or alters gameplay art. A human-approved source and a separately reviewed Asset V2 integration are still required.

sections.heading: The draft has a meaningful release-mode caveat
sections.text: The PR has not passed its requested Godot gameplay smoke tests or security review. Its release-mode opt-in currently uses broader developer flags, so a dedicated inspection-only gate should be considered before wider use.

insights.title: The missing-art backlog could become spatially actionable
insights.explanation: Coordinate-stamped observations would give the art pipeline exact places to repair, connecting playtesting directly to incremental asset installation without automating aesthetic approval.

insights.title: Developer-mode isolation is the key safety gate
insights.explanation: The proposed release opt-in also enables other DevMode features. Separating the inspector's permissions would reduce accidental exposure of unrelated debug capabilities.

article.takeaway: A reviewable implementation candidate now exists, but no gameplay-tested or production-enabled art inspection feature has been established.
article.next_watch: Watch for Godot capture smoke tests, local evidence privacy review, dedicated release gating and an independent acceptance decision.
